key_insight: Reactive vapor–liquid equilibrium changes droplet evaporation by coupling reversible chemistry to phase behavior, heat transfer, and mass transfer.
engineering_relevance: Modeling these coupled effects can inform thermal systems that use reactive phase-change fluids to improve thermodynamic performance.
method: Direct numerical simulation of a single droplet evaporating in turbulent flow.
Second-order diffuse-interface framework with two scalar transport equations.
Reactive vapor–liquid equilibrium for the reversible N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂ system.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports altered critical points and saturation lines, interfacial endothermic and exothermic behavior, and turbulence-enhanced mixing and gas–liquid separation, without quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The equilibrium-based, single-droplet results may not generalize to finite-rate chemistry or practical multi-droplet flows without further validation.
paper_title: Reactive Phase Change of a Single Droplet in Turbulent Flow with Reactive Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium Using a Two-Scalar Diffusive-Interface Method
